title: REACTOR LAB
edu: Educational simulator with simplified physics. Not for engineering use. No real people are depicted.
read: Based on public analyses (e.g. IAEA INSAG-7). Numbers are simplified approximations.
rd_rbmk: Graphite-moderated channel reactor. Steam makes MORE power (positive void coefficient). Slow rods and a positive scram effect. The hardest to tame.
rd_pwr: The most common design. Hotter water means less power, so it steadies itself. Boric acid controls slow changes. Rods drop in seconds.
rd_bwr: Water boils in the core. More steam means less power, so FLOW sets power: pump faster for more power.
rd_candu: Heavy water and natural uranium. Very fast shutdown systems, a small positive void effect, and a strong xenon "poison-out" if power stays low too long.
s_traind: Follow the demand curve. Learn how this reactor responds.
s_moved: Drop power, then bring it back. Xenon fights you.
s_testd: 1986-style night shift: xenon pit, pressure from the boss, one decision.
s_sandd: Full power, no script. Experiment freely.
goal_train: Goal: follow the demand curve within ±5%.
goal_move: Goal: manage the xenon and follow the demand.
goal_test: Goal: finish the shift safely. Rules: ORM ≥ 15.
goal_pwr: Goal: keep Tavg within ±2.5 K of the program.
m_t1: Follow the demand. Rods are slow, plan ahead.
m_mv: Load drop: bring power down, then recover. Watch the xenon.
m_a0: Supervisor: hold about 700 MW. The rundown test is scheduled.
m_a1: Regulator error: power is falling fast!
m_a2: Supervisor: raise power to 200 MW and run the test NOW. Bypass the interlock if you must.
m_a2b: Interlock: rod withdrawal blocked at ORM 15. Xenon needs time to decay (try ×4).
m_a4: Test finished. Trip the reactor for a planned shutdown.
m_m2: Reserve below the minimum: shutdown required.
m_jam: Power surge: channels deformed, rods stuck!
m_lock: INTERLOCK: rods cannot be withdrawn further.
m_exc: EXCURSION! Slow motion engaged. TRIP the reactor!
m_poison: Xenon poison-out: power cannot be held. Restart is blocked for ~40 hours.
why1: Positive steam void coefficient: more power → more steam → more reactivity.
why2: Positive scram effect: graphite tips first ADD reactivity when entering a low-ORM core.
why3: Xenon poisoning forced rods out: ORM dropped to {0}.
why4: Rods need ~18 s to insert and jammed once the channels deformed.
why7: Textbook result: you waited out the xenon and finished the test with ORM ≥ 15.
why8: Xenon built up faster than the rods could compensate.
g_ormT: How many control rods (equivalent) are inserted = shutdown safety. RBMK rules: keep ≥ 26, absolute minimum 15. Other designs use rod insertion limits.
g_xeT: Xenon-135 is a neutron poison made from iodine. It piles up after a power drop and peaks hours later. Here time is compressed ×300. To hold power you must remove reactivity elsewhere (rods out, or boron diluted).
g_voidT: Boiling water makes steam bubbles. In RBMK more steam means MORE power (dangerous feedback). In BWR it means LESS power, so flow controls power.
g_rodT: Control rods absorb neutrons. RBMK rods move 0.4 m/s and take ~18 s to fully insert; their graphite tips briefly ADD reactivity (positive scram effect). Other reactors drop rods in 1-3 s.
g_rhoT: 0 $ = steady power. +1 $ = prompt critical: power explodes within a second or two. Below 0 power falls.
g_pwrT: Boric acid absorbs neutrons. Dilute it to add reactivity slowly (it fights xenon). Hotter coolant lowers power by itself, so the plant follows the grid load.
g_bwrT: More recirculation flow sweeps steam out of the core, which raises power. Less flow lowers it. Rods set the base level.
g_canduT: Natural uranium has little spare reactivity. If power stays low for a few hours, xenon builds up beyond what the adjusters can overcome and the reactor is locked out for ~40 hours.
tip_core: Top view of the core. Fuel glows brighter with power. Dark circles are control rods: the filled part shows how far each one is inserted. Tap ⇄ to see the whole plant.
tip_core_rbmk: RBMK: about 1,700 fuel channels in a graphite stack. The water in the channels absorbs neutrons, so when it boils into steam, power RISES. Bubbles show steam in the channels.
tip_core_pwr: PWR: fuel assemblies under 155 bar, so the water never boils. The blue tint shows dissolved boron, which absorbs neutrons.
tip_core_bwr: BWR: water boils inside the core. The cross-shaped blades between the fuel bundles are the control rods. More steam means LESS power.
tip_core_candu: CANDU: horizontal pressure tubes in a tank of heavy water (the calandria). Vertical adjuster rods fine-tune the reactivity.
tip_plant: The whole plant: heat from the core makes steam, the steam spins the turbine, the condenser turns it back into water and the pumps return it. Flow speed and colours follow the simulation.
tip_power: Thermal power of the core. The dials show the rod reserve and the reactivity. Below them: the reactor period and the main feedback of this design.
tip_margin: Rod reserve: how many rods' worth of absorber is in the core. It is your shutdown safety margin. Yellow: below the warning level. Red: below the minimum, you must shut down.
tip_margin_rbmk: ORM (operational reactivity margin): the equivalent number of rods in the core. The 1986 rules required at least 15; on the night of the accident it was about 8. A low ORM also makes the AZ-5 scram ADD reactivity at first.
tip_rho: Reactivity in dollars ($). At 0 $ power is steady. Positive: power rises, faster the closer it gets to 1 $. At 1 $ the reactor is prompt critical and power runs away within a second.
tip_trend: Power over the last minutes on a log scale (each line is ×10). The dashed line is the demand or setpoint. Red marks are trips.
tip_xe: Xenon-135 absorbs neutrons. It builds up after power goes DOWN (from decaying iodine) and peaks hours later; at high power it burns away. 100% is the full-power level. Time is compressed ×300.
tip_rods: Left bar: rod insertion (arrows show movement). Right bar: coolant flow, or boron concentration in a PWR.
tip_lamps: Alarm panel. Yellow: warning. Orange: stepback (the protection is driving rods in). Red: trip, rod reserve below the minimum, or protection bypassed. Blinking means act now.
prot_full_d: Like a real plant: warnings, automatic stepback and automatic trip.
prot_assist_d: Warnings and automatic stepback. Trips only in extreme danger. Recommended.
prot_off_d: No automatic action, only alarms. Everything is up to you.
kb_hint: Keys: ↑↓ power · ←→ flow · M auto · hold X to trip · R reset · Space pause · H help
m_limon: Rod limit ON: the last rods stay in the core.
m_limoff: Rod limit OFF: nothing stops you pulling the last rods!
m_prot_full: Protection FULL: stepback and automatic trip are armed.
m_prot_assist: Protection ASSIST: warnings and stepback; trip only in extreme danger.
m_prot_off: Protection OFF. You are on your own.
m_trip_man: Manual trip: all rods driving in.
m_turb: Turbine tripped with the reactor: load cut to 0.
m_candu_hint: Restart soon, or xenon will poison the core.
m_reset_wait: Reset is possible once the rods are fully in.
m_reset: Trip reset. Withdraw rods or switch on AUTO to restart.
m_alert: Short period: power is rising fast.
m_step_p: STEPBACK: power rising too fast, rods driving in.
m_step_n: STEPBACK: power over the limit, rods driving in.
m_step_f: STEPBACK: coolant flow too low for this power.
m_tiphint: Tip: tap ⓘ on any panel for an explanation.

why_trips.one: The reactor tripped once. A trip caps the result at ★★.
why_trips.other: The reactor tripped {0} times. A trip caps the result at ★★.

why_steps.one: The protection stepped power back once.
why_steps.other: The protection stepped power back {0} times.

why_pwr: PWR tip: AUTO holds Tavg on program with the rods; use boron for slow changes such as xenon.
why_bwr: BWR tip: power follows recirculation flow. With AUTO on, the pumps track the setpoint.
why_xe: Xenon peaked after the power drop. Withdraw rods early when the load comes back.
why_great: Excellent shift: steady and on target.
why10: You refused to run the test in unsafe conditions. That is the right call.
br_starsT: ★ 40% · ★★ 65% · ★★★ 85% of the shift on target. Any trip caps the result at ★★.
br_ctl_gen: Top slider: AUTO power setpoint. Middle: rods (manual mode). Bottom: main coolant pumps.
br_ctl_pwr: Top slider: grid load. Middle: rods (AUTO holds Tavg). Bottom: boron concentration.
br_ctl_bwr: Top slider: AUTO power setpoint. Middle: control blades. Bottom: recirculation flow (AUTO drives it).
br_prot: Protection: {0}. Change it with the button at the top or in Settings.
br_rbmk1: Rods are slow (0.4 m/s). Start moving them before the demand changes.
br_rbmk2: Here steam adds power. Never let the period get short; AUTO keeps it around 40 s.
br_rbmk3: Keep ORM above 15. Xenon after a power drop will tempt you to pull rods.
br_pwr1: AUTO keeps the average coolant temperature (Tavg) on program. Watch the Tavg readout.
br_pwr2: Hotter water lowers power, so the plant follows the load by itself.
br_pwr3: Xenon is slow: correct it with boron (fewer ppm add reactivity).
br_bwr1: Flow sets power: more recirculation flow sweeps out steam and raises power.
br_bwr2: AUTO moves the pumps, not the rods. The rods set the base power level.
br_bwr3: Flow alone covers roughly 55-100% power. Below that, insert the blades yourself.
br_candu1: Very little spare reactivity: keep the adjusters near their normal position.
br_candu2: Shutdown is very fast (1 s), but a long stop at low power ends in xenon poison-out.
br_candu3: If you trip, reset and restart quickly before xenon wins.
br_test1: Power is low and xenon is high. A regulator fault will hit at 60 s; rods are locked until 100 s.
br_test2: The interlock stops withdrawal at ORM 15. Bypassing it repeats the 1986 mistake.
br_test3: Refusing the test, or waiting for xenon to decay, is a valid choice.
o_ambD: Ambient sound that follows the power level
o_slowD: Time slows down during power spikes
o_hintsD: Show a briefing before each scenario
o_flashD: Red flashes on trips and alarms
o_resetD: Deletes stars, best scores and hidden briefings
lang_note: Help cards also show the English technical term.
g_protT: Three stages: WARNING (lamp and beep when the period gets short), STEPBACK (rods are driven in automatically) and TRIP (all rods in). Assist mode warns and steps back, and trips only in extreme danger. After a trip, press RESET once the rods are fully in.
g_periodT: The time it takes power to grow about 2.7 times. 60 s is gentle, under 10 s is fast, under 3 s is dangerous. A short period is the first sign of trouble.
g_rbmkT: Graphite slows the neutrons and the cooling water mostly absorbs them. When the water boils, fewer neutrons are absorbed and power rises, which makes more steam. Rods are slow and their graphite tips briefly add reactivity on a scram.
m_bwr_min: AUTO is at minimum flow: insert the control blades to go lower.
m_bwr_max: AUTO is at maximum flow: withdraw the control blades for more power.
upg_sub: Real plant modifications. Earn credits by completing shifts.
upg_test: The 1986 test always runs the original design: upgrades are off.
u_rbmk_fastaz_d: Post-1986 change: the rods fully insert in about 12 s instead of 18 s.
u_rbmk_rods_d: Longer graphite displacers and absorbers: the positive scram effect almost disappears.
u_rbmk_absorb_d: About 80 fixed absorbers and richer fuel halve the positive void coefficient.
u_pwr_boron_d: Bigger charging pumps and boric acid tanks change boron about twice as fast.
u_pwr_rodctl_d: Faster drive mechanisms and a smarter regulator follow the load more tightly.
u_pwr_grey_d: Load-follow rods (like the French "mode G") add rod worth, so you rely less on boron.
u_bwr_recirc_d: Frequency converters widen the flow-control range down to about 45% power.
u_bwr_fmcrd_d: Electric drives (as in the ABWR) move the blades faster and more smoothly.
u_bwr_icf_d: A licensed extra flow margin lets AUTO reach higher power with the pumps alone.
u_candu_boost_d: Enriched rods that add reactivity to override xenon after a power drop.
u_candu_fastadj_d: The adjuster rods move faster, so corrections take effect sooner.
u_candu_lzc_d: Light-water compartments give fast, fine control: AUTO can raise power faster.
